text.en: Believing a thin-walled member under compression fails once its stress reaches the material's compressive strength, the same way a thick, stocky member does -- thin-walled compression members typically fail by buckling, a sudden sideways instability, at a critical load that can be far below what the material's actual compressive strength would allow; the member's geometry (slenderness, thickness, stiffening, support conditions) sets this critical load, not material strength alone.
text.et: Arvamus, et õhukeseseinaline surve all olev element murdub, kui selle pinge jõuab materjali survetugevuseni, samamoodi nagu paks, jäme element -- õhukeseseinalised survekoormatud elemendid murduvad tavaliselt pahklumise, järsu külgsuunalise ebastabiilsuse tõttu, kriitilisel koormusel, mis võib olla palju madalam sellest, mida materjali tegelik survetugevus lubaks; elemendi geomeetria (sihvakus, paksus, jäigastus, toestustingimused) määrab selle kriitilise koormuse, mitte materjali tugevus üksi.
